newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy committed to mini-budget if needed - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy committed to mini-budget if needed - Prodi.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he would have no hesitation in drawing a supplementary budget for 1997 if additional measures were needed to keep Italy's public deficit under control.
In a speech to the congress of the Popular Party, a partner in his centre-left coalition, he also reaffirmed that any measures would consist of spending cuts.
"If it, a new adjustment budget, should prove necessary next spring, and I still hope it will not be necessary, the government will not hesitate to draft it," Prodi said.

"I have also said, however, that if a budget is needed, it will be on the spending side. Our attention in future action on economic policy must be primarily focused on structural reforms to spending and to its most severe control," he said.

Prodi has drawn up a tough and unpopular 62.5-trillion lire budget for 1997, which is heavy on additional revenue, to try to keep the deficit in check and boost Italy's chances of membership in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Odds have shortened on additional measures being needed in coming months after official estimates showed the 1996 deficit at 138.5 trillion lire against a target 123.0 trillion.
